source.title: Gradient Descent Finds Global Minima of Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: S. Du; J. Lee; Hao-Chuan Li; Li-Wei Wang; Xi-Yu Zhai

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent cutoff affecting the study’s results.
record.tranche_reason: The paper theoretically analyzes whether gradient descent can reach zero training loss on arbitrary bounded labels, rather than empirically training networks on random labels as in the original studies.
record.gate_note: The paper’s own convergence theorems bear on fitting arbitrary labels. Its introduction cites the original random-label finding, but those cited results are not recorded as rows. It does not report test error, chance-level test performance, or experiments with random labels.
record.test_reason: Theorems 5.1–7.1 prove convergence to zero training loss for arbitrary bounded labels, which include completely random labels. This tests V1's fitting component through theoretical analysis under specified assumptions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors prove convergence to zero training loss for sufficiently overparameterized deep networks under their assumptions. They leave test loss and stochastic gradient descent unaddressed, and explicitly identify coverage of practical network widths as an open problem.
record.recipe_differences: The original sources report empirical random-label experiments; this paper proves gradient-descent convergence under theoretical assumptions. Its ResNet uses skip connections at every layer and explicit residual scaling, and its analysis is for gradient descent rather than stochastic gradient descent.
record.method_sensitivity: Theorems require architecture-specific width and step-size conditions; the fully-connected network has exponential dependence on depth in the stated bounds, while the residual-network bounds are polynomial. The authors identify activation, data non-degeneracy, and architecture assumptions.
record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2018; proceedings volume dated 2019 in the supplied text)
record.problems: The evidence is theoretical rather than empirical. The authors state that test loss is not addressed, that the analysis covers gradient descent rather than stochastic gradient descent, and that the required widths are still very large for ResNet and may not cover commonly used networks. The network assumptions include smooth analytic non-polynomial activations and non-degenerate inputs.
record.rows_left_out: No additional own results directly measuring the claim’s random-label behavior were identified. The random-label observation in the introduction is attributed to Zhang et al. and is cited prior work, not a result of this study.

untested.parts: Chance-level test error, stochastic gradient training, applicability to standard practical widths, and fitting random labels without changing the architecture or hyperparameters used for true labels are not established.
Relative training time for true versus random labels and slowing convergence with increasing corruption.
The specified shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel and Gaussian-noise input settings.
Training and test behavior across a label-corruption sweep, including steadily increasing test error.
Effects of weight decay, dropout and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Whether shared real-data patterns are learned before noisy labels.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's limits_scope verdict: untested components and sufficient theorem assumptions do not demonstrate failures outside those assumptions. The supplied proceedings attribution is ICML 2019, not ICML 2018.

versions.untested_parts: Does not explicitly sample random labels or measure test error at chance. Studies gradient descent, not stochastic gradient methods, and does not compare with true-label generalization or establish that the architectures and hyperparameters match standard empirical settings.
No comparison of training time for true versus random labels, or sweep over corrupted-label fractions.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiments.
No label-noise sweep or test-error measurement.
No weight-decay, dropout, or data-augmentation comparison.
No comparison of learning real-label patterns with memorizing noise over training.

rows.subject: deep fully-connected neural network
rows.size_stated: width m = Ω(2^O(H) max{n⁴/(λmin(K(H))⁴δ), n² log(Hn/δ)/(λmin(K(H))²), n⁴/λmin(K(H))²})
rows.operation_detail: Theorem gives a gradient-descent training-loss convergence bound for the specified network and bounded labels.
rows.uncertainty: with probability at least 1 − δ over random initialization
rows.note: The theorem states convergence to the global minimum and zero training loss for sufficiently large width. The label condition is bounded magnitude; the theorem does not report a random-label experiment.
rows.check: Retain as a theoretical guarantee, not an empirical observation. Add the activation assumptions and positive minimum Gram eigenvalue; Proposition F.1 establishes positivity for nonparallel inputs. Zero loss is the convergence limit.

rows.subject: ResNet
rows.size_stated: width m as specified in Theorem 6.1; polynomial in n, H and the stated data-dependent quantities
rows.operation_detail: Theorem gives a gradient-descent training-loss convergence bound for the specified residual network and bounded labels.
rows.uncertainty: with probability at least 1 − δ over random initialization
rows.note: The theorem states convergence to the global minimum and zero training loss for sufficiently large width. The authors note this architecture differs from standard ResNet: skip connections are at every layer, with explicit residual scaling.
rows.check: Retain as a theoretical guarantee. Add the activation assumptions and positive minimum Gram eigenvalue, established for nonparallel inputs in Proposition F.2. The architecture uses explicitly scaled residual branches and skip connections at every layer. Zero loss is the convergence limit.

rows.subject: convolutional ResNet
rows.size_stated: width m as specified in Theorem 7.1; polynomial in n, p, H and the stated data-dependent quantities
rows.operation_detail: Theorem gives a gradient-descent training-loss convergence bound for the specified convolutional residual network and bounded labels.
rows.uncertainty: with probability at least 1 − δ over random initialization
rows.note: The theorem states convergence to the global minimum and zero training loss for sufficiently large width. This is a theoretical result, not a reported experiment.
rows.check: Retain as a theoretical guarantee conditional on the activation assumptions and a positive minimum Gram eigenvalue. Zero loss is the convergence limit. The step-size formula is poorly rendered in the supplied theorem text; Lemma D.6 states a sufficient bound proportional to λ0 H²/n² times poly(1/p), rather than the row's λ0² dependence.

source_check.correct: The step-size condition is η = O(λ0 H²/(n² poly(p))), with λ0 = λmin(K(H)); λ0 is not squared.
source_check.locator_found: Theorem 7.1; Appendix opening definition of λ0; Lemmas D.6–D.7.
source_check.problem: The step-size formula incorrectly squares λ0; the proof explicitly gives linear dependence on λ0.
